name: Oracle Health Foundation — Pediatric Medical Case Grants
description: The Oracle Health Foundation provides individual case grants for children worldwide who need medical procedures their families cannot afford. Grants cover a wide range of pediatric needs including organ transplants, heart surgeries, prosthetics, wheelchairs, hearing aids, eyeglasses, and other critical medical interventions. The foundation partners with hospitals and medical facilities globally to arrange treatment and directly funds procedures for children in need. International patients are eligible and the program has served children from dozens of countries, making it a significant resource for emigrant families whose children require specialized care not available or affordable in their home country.
eligibility: Children under 18 worldwide who require medical treatment their families cannot afford; no citizenship or immigration status restrictions; families must demonstrate financial need and provide medical documentation of the child's condition
amount: Varies by case — covers full or partial cost of medical procedures including surgeries, prosthetics, and assistive devices
targetDiagnosis: Pediatric conditions requiring surgical or medical intervention: congenital heart defects, organ failure, limb deficiencies, hearing loss, vision impairment, orthopedic conditions
applicationProcess: Submit an application through the Oracle Health Foundation website detailing the child's medical condition and financial situation. Applications are reviewed by the foundation's medical and grants team. If approved, the foundation coordinates directly with medical facilities to arrange treatment and payment. A medical professional must provide documentation of the child's diagnosis and recommended treatment plan.
geographicScope: International — children from any country may apply; treatment arranged at partner hospitals worldwide
documentsRequired: Medical records and diagnosis from treating physician; letter of recommendation from medical professional; proof of financial need; child's identification documents; treatment plan and cost estimate from receiving hospital

name: Shriners Children's — International Patient Financial Assistance Program
description: Shriners Children's operates a network of pediatric specialty hospitals across North America that provide care regardless of a family's ability to pay or insurance status. The system specializes in orthopedic conditions, burns, spinal cord injuries, and cleft lip and palate. International patients are actively accepted, with dedicated international patient coordinators who help families navigate travel, visa requirements, and treatment logistics. Shriners Children's has treated children from over 170 countries since its founding. For emigrant families and international patients, the program offers a critical pathway to world-class pediatric specialty care that may not be available in their home countries, with all financial barriers removed.
eligibility: Children under 18 with orthopedic conditions, burns, spinal cord injuries, cleft lip/palate, or other conditions treatable within the Shriners system; no insurance, citizenship, or immigration status requirements; care provided regardless of family's ability to pay
amount: Full cost of treatment covered — no out-of-pocket expense for qualifying patients regardless of insurance status
targetDiagnosis: Orthopedic conditions (clubfoot, scoliosis, osteogenesis imperfecta, limb deficiencies), burns and burn reconstruction, spinal cord injuries, cleft lip and palate, other pediatric subspecialties
applicationProcess: Families can request an appointment through the Shriners Children's website or by calling the patient referral line. An international patient coordinator assists with the process for families outside the US. A physician referral is helpful but not always required. The medical team reviews the child's condition to determine if treatment can be provided within their system. If accepted, the coordinator helps arrange travel and accommodation logistics.
geographicScope: International — patients from any country accepted; 22 hospital locations across the United States, Canada, and Mexico
documentsRequired: Medical records and diagnosis; physician referral letter (recommended); child's identification or passport; any available imaging or test results; completed patient intake form

name: Southwest Airlines Medical Transportation Grant Program
description: The Southwest Airlines Medical Transportation Grant Program provides complimentary round-trip airline tickets to patients who need to travel for medical treatment but cannot afford the cost of airfare. The program partners with qualified nonprofit medical transportation organizations to distribute tickets to patients in need. This is particularly valuable for immigrant and emigrant families in the United States who may need to travel to specialized medical centers far from their home city but lack the financial resources for airfare. The program supports patients of all ages traveling for a wide range of medical conditions, from cancer treatment to organ transplants to specialty consultations.
eligibility: Patients of any age who need to travel for medical treatment and cannot afford airfare; must be referred through a qualified nonprofit medical transportation partner organization; travel must be within the Southwest Airlines domestic route network
amount: Complimentary round-trip airline tickets — value varies by route (typically $200–$800 per round trip)
targetDiagnosis: Any medical condition requiring travel to a distant treatment center — cancer, organ transplant, rare diseases, pediatric specialty care, clinical trials
applicationProcess: Patients cannot apply directly to Southwest Airlines. Instead, apply through one of the program's nonprofit partner organizations (such as Mercy Medical Angels, Corporate Angel Network, or other qualifying medical transport charities). The partner organization verifies the medical need and submits the ticket request to Southwest Airlines on the patient's behalf.
geographicScope: United States — domestic Southwest Airlines routes only (covers most major US cities)
documentsRequired: Medical documentation confirming need for treatment at a distant facility; proof of financial need; referral from a qualified nonprofit medical transportation partner; valid government-issued ID for travel

name: Mercy Medical Angels — Free Medical Transport for Patients in Need
description: Mercy Medical Angels (formerly Medical Missions) is a national nonprofit organization that provides free transportation services to patients who need to travel for medical care but cannot afford the cost. The organization coordinates volunteer pilots, commercial airline tickets, long-distance ground transportation, and gas reimbursement to help patients reach treatment facilities. Mercy Medical Angels serves patients with both common and rare diseases across all 50 US states. For immigrant and low-income families who may live far from specialty medical centers or cancer treatment facilities, this program removes the transportation barrier that often prevents patients from receiving life-saving care.
eligibility: Patients in the United States who are financially distressed and need to travel more than 50 miles for medical treatment; must have a confirmed medical appointment; all medical conditions considered; no citizenship requirement but must be located within the US
amount: Free transportation — includes volunteer pilot flights, commercial airline tickets, long-distance ground transport, and gas reimbursement depending on availability and distance
targetDiagnosis: Any medical condition requiring travel to a distant treatment facility — serves patients with both common and rare diseases
applicationProcess: Submit a transportation request through the Mercy Medical Angels website or by calling their patient services line. Provide documentation of your medical appointment and financial need. A case coordinator reviews the request and matches the patient with available transportation resources — volunteer pilot flights for shorter distances, commercial airline tickets, or ground transport depending on the route and timing. Requests should be submitted at least 2 weeks before the appointment date.
geographicScope: United States — all 50 states; transportation to medical facilities nationwide
documentsRequired: Confirmed medical appointment documentation; proof of financial need; valid photo ID; medical records or physician letter confirming diagnosis and treatment plan; completed patient application form

name: Global Medical Relief Fund — Medical Care for Children Worldwide
description: The Global Medical Relief Fund (GMRF) is a nonprofit organization that provides free medical care to children injured or ill from wars, natural disasters, and disease in countries with limited medical resources. Founded in 1997, GMRF brings children from around the world to the United States for treatment including prosthetic limbs, reconstructive surgery, and other specialized medical care. The organization covers all costs including travel, medical treatment, and temporary housing with volunteer host families during recovery. GMRF has served children from over 40 countries, making it a vital resource for emigrant communities and families in conflict-affected regions whose children need medical interventions unavailable locally.
eligibility: Children under 18 from countries with inadequate medical resources who have been injured or made ill by war, natural disaster, or disease; the child's condition must be treatable in the United States; no financial means to obtain treatment independently
amount: Full coverage — all medical treatment costs, travel, accommodation with host families, and follow-up care provided at no cost to the family
targetDiagnosis: War injuries, natural disaster injuries, conditions requiring prosthetics, reconstructive surgery, orthopedic conditions, burns, and other pediatric conditions treatable in the US
applicationProcess: Referrals are accepted from medical professionals, NGOs, and community organizations worldwide. Contact GMRF through their website or by phone to initiate a case. The organization's medical team evaluates whether the child's condition is treatable and arranges all logistics including visa support, travel, host family placement, and hospital scheduling. Cases are prioritized based on medical urgency and the lack of local treatment options.
geographicScope: International — children from any country with inadequate medical resources; treatment provided in the United States (primarily New York area hospitals)
documentsRequired: Medical records and diagnosis documentation; referral from medical professional or NGO; child's identification or passport; photographs of the child's condition; letter from local physician confirming treatment is unavailable locally
